conventions.verify_probe: Same convention as 04-build-plan/backlog.json: 'pnpm probe <path>' runs probes/<path>.probe.ts, a Tier 0 file written before the implementation row starts and never edited by the agent doing the row. Every probe fails today because its target does not exist (a missing probe file exits 2, a missing behaviour exits 1). The probe pack for a milestone is committed by the Owner or a pair session before the milestone's rows start.
conventions.status: All rows start as open. Status lives only in the ledger database (imported with fw ledger sync), never in prose.
conventions.size: S under one agent session (about 150 changed lines), M one to two sessions, L split if it exceeds 600 changed lines or three sessions.
conventions.gate: owner-approval means the Owner must approve the PR through the code-owner path before merge (Tier 0 touch, credential, policy, budget or promotion).
conventions.origin: 'full-plan row, included' keeps id, title, epic, priority, size, lane, description, acceptance and verify_probe of 04-build-plan/backlog.json; files_hint is rewritten to the Core package layout (full_files_hint keeps the original), depends_on is re-pointed at rows present in Core (full_depends_on keeps the original) and core_adaptation says what is narrower. 'new Core row' names the full-plan rows it replaces or merges in derived_from.
conventions.phase: Phase in the full plan that the row belongs to (or its earliest derived_from row). core_milestone is the Core milestone: C0, C1 or C2.

C0.name: Walking skeleton
C0.exit_demo: From a clean clone, on a real repo with a real vendor: fw ledger sync; fw run start <row> opens a PR whose comment carries the evidence bundle hash, the probe passed on the branch, the cost record is under the row cap and fw audit verify is green. The Owner merges the PR by hand; fw ledger close <row> runs the probe on the merged artifact and the row becomes done with a post-merge evidence bundle.

C1.name: Safe loop
C1.exit_demo: fwd is running. A row goes to a Claude maker in the sandbox and a Codex verifier (different vendor); a decision card appears (fw inbox); fw approve binds to the head SHA; the merge slot is granted and the daemon merges with expected-head; the reconciler confirms the landing; the watch window closes and the row is done. Then three drills: push after approval (slot and approval void, nothing merges), fw kill mid-run (run halted, leases revoked, even with fwd stopped), and a budget breach (run killed, next dispatch refused).

C2.name: Daily driver
C2.exit_demo: At 06:00 the digest stream publishes the Dawn Log. In the browser (paired, loopback) the Owner reads it, clears three cards in the Captain's Table (approve a merge with the evidence view open, choose from scan findings, answer a question), sees Table cleared, browses Projects, ledger, Runs and Spend, presses the Kill switch in a drill and resumes. A prompt composed for a vendor that cannot be driven headlessly is pasted back and ingested (relay-assist).

rows.title: A crash never leaves a flow cycle's vendor running
rows.description: A clean fwd stop already kills a running flow cycle's vendor (FW-C-038), but a crash or a kill -9 leaves it running with nothing watching it, still spending the Owner's plan until its wall clock ends, and the cycle never gets a report. Cycles are not ledger runs, so the startup reconciler does not know them. When a cycle's vendor starts, fwd records its process group in the cycle folder ($FW_HOME/flows/<key>/cycles/<fire>/vendor.json with pgid and started_at) and removes that record once the cycle's report is written. On start, before the scheduler runs, fwd finds every cycle folder that still holds a vendor.json, kills that process group the same way the reconciler kills a crashed run's group (killOrphanGroup: only when a live member's working directory is inside that cycle folder, so a reused group id is never signalled), writes the cycle's run report with outcome failed and a reason that starts "orphaned", and removes the record, so a second start writes nothing more.

Add three routes under /v1/supervisor, CLI token only: GET /v1/supervisor/flows/{key}/drafts lists the flow's draft files ($FW_HOME/flows/<key>/drafts/), newest first, with id, fire_id, lead_id, channel, subject, body, status and held. POST .../drafts/{id}/approve hands that one draft off exactly as Autopilot does (the same outbox file and one notification.queued event, deduplicated on the same key, so approving twice changes nothing) and marks it handed_off with approved_at. It is refused with 409 and a reason when the flow is at Draft (needs_copilot: at Draft the Owner sends by hand), when the draft was rejected, when it is a template or has no lead, when its channel is not one of the flow's, or when the kill switch or the Supervisor pause is on. POST .../drafts/{id}/reject marks it rejected; a rejected draft is never handed off. The CLI gains fw supervisor drafts <flow>, fw supervisor approve <flow> <id> and fw supervisor reject <flow> <id>, each with --json. Showing these drafts on the web Flows page is a later row.

rows.title: The email sender never sends one message twice when Gmail's answer is lost
rows.description: An audit on 10 Nov found that senders/email.mjs treats a timeout or a dropped connection after the message text as temporary and tries the item again. If Gmail kept the message but its answer never arrived, the organizer gets the same message twice, which is the thing the sender promises never to do. A connection the server closes without a word also leaves the pass waiting forever. The sender writes a line for the item to sent.jsonl just before it hands over the message text, so from then on the item and its address count as written to. A confirmed send moves to sent/ as before. A drop or timeout after the message text moves the item to failed/ with a reason that says it may have been delivered, so the Owner can check his Sent folder; it is never tried again. A drop before the message text still leaves the item for a later pass, and every pass ends.
acceptance: A drop after the message text moves the item to failed/ saying it may have been delivered, and sent.jsonl names it
A drop at RCPT leaves the item in the outbox and it sends on the next pass
A new item to an address whose answer was lost is skipped; that address receives the message text exactly once
A pass ends on its own when the server closes the connection without answering

rows.title: Hunts skip organizers in the EU, the UK and Canada, and label each draft with how to send it
rows.description: On 10 Nov the Owner said hunts must follow the rules, and asked to send each message the way the organizer can be reached. The cycle brief asks the adapter for country, contact_via and contact_url.

rows.title: Paid ads flow: see what the Google Ads campaign spends and what each subscription costs
rows.description: The Owner runs a Google Ads campaign for Frequency (Find your people locally, goal: subscriptions) and nothing in FlowWeb shows it. Ship a read-only flow, paid-ads, in the Frequency project: flows/paid-ads/ (stream, config, project), daemon logic that reads the campaign's daily numbers and decides a next move, GET /v1/flows/paid-ads, and a section on the web Flows page. Daily numbers come from Google Ads campaign report CSVs the Owner drops into $FW_HOME/flows/paid-ads/imports/ (title lines, then a header row with Day, Campaign, Impr., Clicks, Cost, Conversions; amounts may carry commas). Rows for other campaigns are ignored; a later day's file replaces an earlier one's numbers for the same day. The view gives totals and last-7-days figures (spend, impressions, clicks, CTR, cost per click, subscriptions, cost per subscription) and one next move: waiting_for_data with no rows, learning while fewer than learning_days days have data, check_tracking when spend has reached check_tracking_multiple times the target cost per subscription with zero subscriptions, over_target when cost per subscription is above target, on_target otherwise. The flow never changes the campaign, its budget or its bids: it holds no ad account credential and its stream has no outward action class. Pulling the same numbers automatically from Google Analytics is a later row.

rows.description: On 10 Nov the Owner asked for flows that learn: every flow should track its results and shift toward what works. A flow cannot learn from its drafts today. rows.title: Each week the flow scores its hunts and shifts effort toward what works, as far as the dial allows
rows.description: On 10 Nov the Owner asked for flows that keep analyzing their results and shifting the campaign. With drafts marked sent and replied, and outcomes pulled from Frequency per draft, fwd can now tell which hunts work. rows.description: The paid ads flow (FW-C-053) only knows what the Owner exports from Google Ads by hand, and the Owner wants tracking hooked up automatically. rows.title: The daily digest runs by itself, and the Console shows it
rows.description: FW-C-023 built the digest (publishDigest checks every line against registered queries before storing it), but nothing calls it and no digest stream is registered, so the Console always says "No digest yet for today". fwd now registers one active stream with key digest and template digest for each project that has a ledger (a backlog-dev stream), on a daily cron at 06:00 in the machine's time zone with catch_up run_once. Each fire publishes that project's digest over the period since its last one (a day for the first). When fwd starts and the project has no digest since the newest slot (the machine was off or asleep at 06:00, or the stream is new), fwd fires the stream once right away, so the Console has today's digest without waiting a day; a restart with today's digest in place publishes nothing. Fires go through the scheduler, so each one is on the job ledger as stream.fired. The Console treats a stored daily report as one that passed its check, since publishDigest stores no other kind and status-report.json has no room for a self_check field. A digest that fails its check is still never stored (digest.rejected).

rows.title: The Owner sets when a flow runs each morning and how many people it reaches a day, and can let reply rates tune that number
rows.description: A flow's run time is fixed in its shipped stream.json (neighborhood activation runs at 07:00 on weekdays) and how many new people a run reaches is only each hunt's max_sends plus the weekly cap, so the Owner cannot run the flow earlier to catch organizers early, run it every day, or turn its intensity up or down, and nothing ties that number to whether people reply. fwd gains POST /v1/supervisor/flows/{key}/schedule { time: 'HH:MM', days: 'daily' | 'weekdays' }, which stores the choice in the Supervisor settings and rewrites the flow's stream trigger cron (version + 1, a new definition_hash and a stream.updated event) so the scheduler fires at the new time; a flow whose stream is not registered yet gets the time when it is. fwd gains POST /v1/supervisor/flows/{key}/intensity { per_day: 1-25, auto: boolean, min, max } (min <= per_day <= max). Each run drafts for at most that many new people a day (counted over the last 20 hours, so the next morning starts fresh); the weekly cap and each hunt's max_sends still apply. rows.title: Launch safety: batch approve refuses blocked, do-not-contact and restricted drafts, an opt-out reaches waiting drafts, links go only to live pages, calendar fetches stay public
rows.description: Fixes from the launch-machine audit of 2026-11-11. (1) POST /v1/flows/{key}/batch/approve refuses, with a reason each, a draft that is not waiting_for_owner (gate_blocked with the gate's reasons), a draft whose address, page, lead or host is on do-not-contact, and a draft for an EU, UK or Canadian lead; none reaches the outbox. It answers 404 for a flow key that is not shipped before it touches the filesystem. (2) An opt-out (a pasted no in the reply helper, a host.opted_out event) moves that person's waiting drafts in every flow to status do_not_contact. approveDraft refuses (409) and Today leaves off anyone on do-not-contact (the flow's own list and the shared neighborhood-activation list). (3) Live links only: Frequency's /start/host, /start/partner, /for/<niche> and /launch pages are not live yet; /create-a-space, /pricing and /help are. With funnels_live false in a flow's config.json or reply-tree.json, or FW_FUNNELS_LIVE=off in fwd's environment, every generated link to a page that is not live goes to /create-a-space with the same query tags; true keeps today's links. The shipped host-moments config sets it false; neighborhood-activation and its reply tree ship true because existing checks pin /start/host and /for/<niche>. (4) Host-moments notes and local pulse roundup drafts run checkDraft and store the gate result; a blocked one is stored gate_blocked. Heads-up drafts skip hosts on do-not-contact. (5) fetchCalendar resolves the host and refuses private, link-local, unique-local, carrier NAT and multicast addresses (any address the host resolves to), never fetches fwd's own port on loopback, and stops reading a body at its byte cap. (7) The draft gate's region check also blocks Canadian provinces and territories and UK nations and regions by name. (8) Today's Approve email batch shows who it goes to and, after it runs, the held and refused drafts with their reasons. (9) The intake engine refuses to start a paid run when the flow's budget is spent, like the reply engine. utm_source stays flowweb.

rows.title: The Owner runs more than one copy of a flow, each with its own name, config, state, drafts and spend
rows.description: The loop protocol doc (2026-11-11, Build next item 5) and the one-prompt canvas need a second "find yoga teachers" flow beside the first, but fwd runs one copy per engine: ENGINES and every flow module key their state by one fixed flow key. A copy is a new flow key "<base>--<slug>" recorded in the Supervisor settings with copy_of = base. One pure resolver maps a key to its base flow and its home: a shipped flow keeps $FW_HOME, a copy gets $FW_HOME/copies/<key>/, and every engine, cycle, draft and spend path runs the base flow's code against that home, so copies never share leads, drafts, hunts or spend while the engines stay unchanged. POST /v1/supervisor/flows/{base}/copy { slug?, name?, note?, config? } makes one (CLI token or paired session): slug defaults to the next free number from 2; config is a shallow patch over the base flow's effective config, limited to keys it already has, written as the copy's config.json override. A copy of a copy, and copies of host-moments, local-pulse and email-queue (fixed templates or one shared queue), are refused. GET /v1/supervisor lists copies beside shipped flows with copy_of (null on shipped ones). Enable, disable, dial, edit, archive, restore, schedule, intensity, AI account, run and the drafts routes all take a copy's key; turning a copy on registers its own stream (its key, a stream id derived from it), its run report names the copy's key, and fwd reaps a crashed copy's cycle like any other. Deleting a copy is archive for now; the site, relay and Flows page buttons are a later row.

rows.title: The Owner sees tokens and dollars per outcome for every flow, from a meter on every model turn
rows.description: Item 1 of Build next in the loop protocol doc (2026-11-11). Daniel: minimal spend means the most effective way to get each result, not the cheapest run, so the deciding number is tokens and dollars per outcome, per flow and per model. Today fwd records a cycle's dollars and input and output tokens in spend_entries (not its cached tokens) and nothing says which flow, step or item a turn was for. fwd now meters every model turn it starts for a flow (a cycle, a draft rewrite, a reply read, an intake read) once, in $FW_HOME/meter/turns.jsonl written only by fwd: at, flow (a copy's own key), step, item (the fire id or the draft id), vendor, model, tokens_in, tokens_cached, tokens_out, usd and the drafts the turn wrote; the cycle's spend_entries row gains its cached tokens. GET /v1/meter/turns?flow&limit lists turns newest first. CLI token or paired session; no flow means every flow.

rows.title: A flow that earns the next dial stop shows as a promotion card the Owner approves, a bad send demotes it at once, and badges come only from real rows
rows.description: The master plan's promotions and badges (2026-11-11), with the trust ladder rule: promotion is slow and Owner-approved, demotion is automatic. Pure promotionFor: Draft to Copilot after 14 days at Draft with at least 20 approved and at most 10% rejected; Copilot to Autopilot after 30 days with no bad send; Autopilot never promotes. A bad send is a sent draft whose person asked not to be contacted, or one the Owner marked a regret. GET /v1/game/badges answers them for this home. Agent cards showing results and cost per result come with the roster. Wave 4 of the master plan v2.
